biomarkers.name: CD20+, CD5-, CD10-, CD23-
biomarkers.clinical_use: Typical immunophenotype; helps distinguish from CLL/SLL (usually CD5+/CD23+), mantle cell lymphoma (usually CD5+/cyclin D1+), and follicular lymphoma (usually CD10+/BCL6+)

biomarkers.name: MYD88 L265P (usually negative)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Helps distinguish from lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma/Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia, which is MYD88 L265P-positive in most cases

biomarkers.name: NOTCH2 mutations
biomarkers.clinical_use: Recurrent in marginal zone lymphoma and supportive of MZL biology, but not specific for nodal MZL

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Small to medium-sized B cells with monocytoid/marginal zone appearance, often with plasmacytic differentiation, infiltrating around reactive follicles of lymph nodes; residual germinal centres may be preserved

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Immunophenotype is typically CD5-, CD10-, and CD23-, helping distinguish from CLL/SLL, mantle cell lymphoma, and follicular lymphoma
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Marginal zone expansion around residual reactive follicles

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Marginal zone B cells — generally considered a post-germinal centre memory B-cell neoplasm
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Marginal zone B-cell differentiation, sometimes with plasmacytic differentiation; CD5-, CD10-, CD23- immunophenotype helps distinguish from CLL/SLL, MCL, and FL
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Marginal zone B-cell lineage retention; recurrent NOTCH2 pathway alterations support marginal zone differentiation biology, but are not present in all cases
